newsitem.title: UK: Mexican Eurobonds surge on U.S./IMF debt repayment.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Eurobonds surge on U.S./IMF debt repayment.

text.p: Spreads on outstanding Mexican Eurobonds tightened by up to 15 basis points on Thursday after it said it would repay the remains of a U.S. loan three years ahead of schedule and repay part of its debt with the IMF.

Mexico's $1.0 billion 10-year global bond, launched last week, was quoted at a 313-309 b.p. yield spread over U.S. Treasuries, down from 323-319 b.p. on Wednesday, dealers said. The deal had already tightened from 335 b.p. over at launch.
Mexico's longest-dated outstanding Eurobonds, its 11.50 percent 2026 bond, came in by 15 b.p. to trade at a 385-382 b.p. spread, dealers said.
"We are very bullish on Mexican debt, and spreads could come in more after today's moves," said a trader at a U.S. bank.
Mexico said on Wednesday it would immediately pay off $3.5 billion owed to the U.S. and would make an early repayment of $1.5 billion to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The loans were part of a near $50 billion package put together by the U.S., the IMF and other countries to avert a global financial disaster during Mexico's peso crisis in 1994.

Although a heavy user of international bond markets in 1996, Mexico's borrowing needs this year are modest. A 500 billion lire 10-year Eurobond scheduled for later this month will complete most of its $1.4 billion requirement, dealers said.
But bankers have not ruled out a further visit to the bond markets to fund another Brady bond buy-back.
"I bet there will be something else coming in the not too distant future," an economist at a European bank said.
Last May Mexico issued an innovative $1.75 billion global bond-for-Bradies swap. In September, it used a $1.0 billion 20-year global bond to buy back more Brady bonds.
Other Latin American borrowers will benefit from the positive mood, dealers said.
Specifically, Argentina was due to launch a $2.0 billion global bond in five- and 20-year tranches next week. Interest in the offering was already strong, dealers said.
"Mexico's recent global was well received and sold to a wide investor base, not just to emerging market investors," said a trader at a European bank.
"This suggests there is good interest in emerging market paper at the moment, and Argentina will benefit," he said.
